title: Bambu Lab X2D Dual-Nozzle 3D Printer Combo with AMS 2 Pro $1249 + Delivery ($0 NSW C&C) @ Mwave
body:
Deal: Bambu Lab X2D Dual-Nozzle 3D Printer Combo with AMS 2 Pro $1249 + Delivery ($0 NSW C&C) @ Mwave

[PeppaCat] looks like 3d printers are much cheaper now, why?
[3dprintdeals] solid 3d printers have been available for a few years starting from $300.
This X2D is a higher end model with a dual nozzle hot end, heating chamber, enclosed & AMS 2 dryer/filament feeder.
[PeppaCat] I remember P series with AMS used to around $1400 and X series with AMS around $1900…. for now looks like they are much cheaper
[3dprintdeals] That was a few years ago, much more competition in the space.
Bambu flagship H series are $2000-3000
[BrotherSharp] @3dprintdeals: Just 1 year ago this was considered the best deal at that time:
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/911693
X1C+AMS2 $2019
P1S+AMS2 $1239
Now a dual nozzle X2D+AMS2 is cheaper than the P1S combo I bought….
[xmessa] It's even cheaper in China—about $740 for the P2S + AMS 2 or $730 for the X2D+ AMS 2. If it weren't for the regional restrictions, I would've bought it from China.
[l4nn13] Would filament be cheaper or worth getting? I can't imagine how you could region lock filament rolls
[xmessa] around 22-30 rmb per 1kg, shipping is 20rmb per 1kg by sea - so that's $9-11 per kg
[cumova] I know google exists. But are there any good guides for kids to learn how to use 3d printers (not on youtube)
[3dprintdeals] First step it to get a printer. The rest is easy to learn as you go.
With Bambu it's even easier to print straight from the app, no slicing on the computer needed.
[fruxo] With bambu, you scroll through millions (?) of models on the app and just print with a single click from the same app. Not really anything to learn besides how to change filament on the printer.
[stuffandthat] Until something goes wrong, or the print fails because the settings don't suit etc. Then it becomes fun!
[3dprintdeals] less likely with the profiels made for the various Bambu machines
[n1x] I recommend learning how to use a 3d modeling software first, like Autodesk Fusion. Once you can design whatever thing you want then you can either print it on your own printer or get someone or a third party to print it for you.
If you just get a 3d printer without any knowledge of 3d models then you are more than likely to just print available free models or buy models to print. Free models will give you plastic junk mostly. Models you design yourself will be priceless and genuinely helpful.
[3dprintdeals] Do both at the same time.
Many problems are already solved by someone else.
Not everything on makerworld is junk, just a lot of the trending models are novelties.
[lovebargain87] Reposting this for others to see:
https://www.jeffgeerling.com/blog/2026/bambu-lab-abusing-ope…
[tangcla] After delivery cost to Melbourne, it's $1333. So almost same price as ordering direct from Bambu.
[3dprintdeals] yes, best for those in Sydney who can pick up from the Auburn store.
[Vladdo] Hard to go past the Snapmaker U1 for the same-ish money.. I'm thoroughly enjoying mine.. no more waste going up in smoke.
[killingtime] Exactly, in 2026 either go cheap or multitool head. These don't make sense anymore
[3dprintdeals] I have the U1 and still see a reason why some would go X2D.
workflow and existing printers
engineering filaments
mainly doing mixed filament for support material
heated chamber & filtration
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Omg should I????
Is four 3d printers too much for 1 person? Hmm
[3dprintdeals] No.. print 4 times aa fast!
Wait.. you have 3 now?
[Jimothy Wongingtons] My old creality still there as a paper weight (works but by comparison it’s a POS). And the a1 and a1m
[RADICALIST] I think the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro is still better since it has 4 print heads?
[3dprintdeals] Different machines.
Creator 5 is great for multicolour but not engineering filaments which need heater chamber and filtration etc.
[tsk2] Pro can be had for 1300 and does … sure there was the minor foxtrot uniform with the purge and fan intake but that appears the be sorted with some minor changes . Ams and single print head is dead unless you just want continuous single colour filament…the sovol m1d looks great and I suspect that some 3d party heating chamber and filter will come. Petg probably meets the requirements for a lot of people and is a shit tonne safer than asa or abs
[3dprintdeals] Multi toolhead printers are definitely the way forward. But for many the X2D is still the machine to get.
I have A1 and U1, sometimes I still print with the A1 because it's just easier
[euk] The 5 pro is definitely suitable for engineering filaments. I feed it PAHT/PPS-CF through a Creality pi4 dryer running at 85 degrees and despite the filament being very stiff it runs beautifully.
These filaments cannot be run through any AMS and hence must be directly fed from a spool outside the AMS system. Due to the nature of nylon it will need to be dried as it's fed into the printer unless you're doing very short prints e.g you'd need a AMS-HT that bypasses the feed motor, but for that cost you might as well get a discounted e.g. Creality pi4 that can do 85 degrees and dry 4 filaments to this temperature at same time.
[3dprintdeals] Nice, waiting for eBay to stock the Creator 5 Pro.
Exciting times
[RADICALIST] Creator 5 Pro has chamber heater and HEPA filter. You can get the C5 Pro for $1249
[Sal in SA] Got one during the sale.
Amazing 3D Printer, for the price would say it is right on.
Also got 10+ filaments during sale.
[3dprintdeals] What sale? X2D wasn't discounted for the anniversary sale
[OZBargainer in SA] It was briefly on sale shortly after it was released until they realised how much of a bargain it was.
[browser] Thanks for sharing, very tempting.
There's no gift card or price beat tricks to go cheaper is there? :D
[3dprintdeals] Best would be 10% off the list price of $1,349 so $1,214.
And that's if Officeworks or JB has stock.
[Inthemix] DOes JP stock the X2D? I thought it was only the P2S
[sonicentropy] Mostly happy with my x2d combo but issues with ptf tub dragging on glass causing print issues. I have had tons of issues with my ams2 too. Sadly my 2 x p1p are way more reliable.
[pisoj1] Has anyone ever found a way to get an AMS2 for cheap?
[Vladdo] Buy a printer with it and sell the printer..?
[SirFaffer] By all means buy this, but don't expect to be printing small multicolour prints. At every colour change it'll poop out a bunch of filament to purge the old colour from the nozzle. You can quite literally end up wasting MANY TIMES as much filament as you use for the print… If you want to do a bunch of multicolour get the snapmaker u1. This is good for dual colour, or using petg supports for pla prints (and vice versa) and printing things like ASA and ABS out of the box, plus nylon etc.
For the purposes that I bought the X2D its excellent, and I've had no problems in 250 hours of print time that weren't my own fault.
The U1 I've just started using today and also so far so good.
[3dprintdeals] Yep, multicolour is not the main purpose for the X2D.
For mixed filament support, it's great. PLA & PETG, PLA & TPU will work great and removing support is such a breeze.
I've got the U1 as well, and I haven't done that many ful multicolour prints yet. Loading & slicing is not as smooth with orcaslicer & snap orca.
[3dprintdeals] yes and no.
servicing it is a pain e.g. TPU clog that requires disassembling the toolhead
It's less automatic than a Bambu since you will have to slice it yourself, but these are things you should learn to do on any 3d printer.
few other things to get used to with the U1 as well like the loading process.
[AlteredBeast] Hmm should I wait for Black Friday sales for the H2D…
[3dprintdeals] did you not look during the Anniversary sale ?
[AlteredBeast] Yeah but didn't need it then 😅
Hopefully also cheaper this year…but this X2D is very enticing…
[3dprintdeals] Always the case
November will be here soon
